reuse.why: All month-wide actions, including the new setLastMonthSpending, go through the existing shouldFillCategory and getAverageFillCategories helpers and the existing averageToBudgetAmount sign helper; setZero, however, writes its own copy of the category query instead of calling getAverageFillCategories.

duplication.why: setZero's new SQL is a verbatim copy of getAverageFillCategories' query (with the same notes join), and the group-notes join is added separately in three queries.

placement.why: Selection rules (templates, #fixed, hidden flag) are added as small predicates inside the single shouldFillCategory definition in budget/actions.ts, and the new action is registered in budget/app.ts alongside its siblings.

scope.why: Changes stay within the month-wide actions, their tests, the handler registration and a type field; collapsing the old 'keep'/'flagged'/'visible' hidden modes into one boolean reaches beyond what the steps ask.

maintainability.why: One predicate now owns every exclusion rule and one optional flag carries the hidden opt-in, which is easy to own; the duplicated category query in setZero and the silently dropped per-action hidden modes are the weak points.

bypasses_abstraction.where: setZero in packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts runs its own copy of the getAverageFillCategories SQL instead of calling the helper

abstraction_drift.where: getAverageFillCategories gains includeHiddenCategories (shouldFillCategory's mode parameter is replaced by a boolean, not added); new exclusion clauses in shouldFillCategory are general rules, not special cases; setZero keeps its own duplicated category query instead of using getAverageFillCategories
